ops.title: synckitd and its helper consumers must upgrade as one era, or the helper socket path splits
ops.body:
A mixed-era hazard specific to synckit's helper model, found while closing out the daemonkit v0.23.0 state-root migration on 2026-08-29. It is not covered by the general "wipe after release" rule, because it breaks a *live* pairing rather than leaving dead directories behind.

## The shape

synckit registers a per-consumer LaunchAgent under a synckit-namespaced label — `internal/serviceidentity/identity.go:33` builds it as `LabelPrefix + ".helper." + name`, giving `com.github.yasyf.synckit.helper.reposync`, `…helper.cookiesync`, `…helper.cc-pool`.

The daemon behind that label is **not** a synckitd process. It is the *consumer's own binary* running as a helper: `reposync/internal/cli/rpcserve.go:11` imports `github.com/yasyf/synckit/helperruntime`. So:

- the **consumer** binary computes the socket path it *serves* on, using the daemonkit version **it** was compiled against;
- **synckitd** computes the socket path it *dials*, using the daemonkit version **it** was compiled against.

daemonkit's state root determines that path, and it moved twice: `~/<label>/` (≤ v0.21.x) → `~/.daemonkit/agents/<label>/` (v0.22.0) → `~/.daemonkit/a/<label>/` (v0.23.0), each time with **no migration and no fallback read**. Two sides compiled against different daemonkit majors therefore look in two different directories and never meet. Nothing errors loudly — the dialer simply finds no socket.

## The evidence

Installed on the workstation at the time of the finding:

| package | version | daemonkit | state root |
|---|---|---|---|
| synckitd | 0.37.2 | v0.21.2 | `~/<label>/` |
| reposync | 0.28.0 | v0.21.2 | `~/<label>/` |
| cookiesync | 0.28.0 | v0.21.2 | `~/<label>/` |
| cc-pool | 0.66.0 | v0.22.0 | `~/.daemonkit/agents/<label>/` |

The matched pairs worked and the mismatched pair did not, exactly as predicted:

- `~/com.github.yasyf.synckit.helper.reposync/` — holds `daemon.sock`. Live.
- `~/com.github.yasyf.synckit.helper.cookiesync/` — holds `daemon.sock`. Live.
- `~/com.github.yasyf.synckit.helper.cc-pool/` — `daemon.records` only, **no `daemon.sock`**.
- `~/.daemonkit/agents/com.github.yasyf.synckit.helper.cc-pool/` — `daemon.records` only, **no `daemon.sock`**.

cc-pool had moved to the v0.22.0 root while synckitd stayed on v0.21.2, so the cc-pool helper pairing was already silently dead — two directories, neither carrying a socket, and no error anywhere naming the split.

## The rule

**synckitd and every consumer that runs as a synckit helper (reposync, cookiesync, cc-pool) upgrade together, in one batch, across a daemonkit state-root move.** Upgrading synckitd alone is the failure case: it starts dialing the new root while its helpers still serve the old one, taking down pairings that currently work.

This also means a partial fleet upgrade is not a safe halfway house. During the v0.23.0 rollout the correct order was: hold synckitd at its old version until reposync and cookiesync had *released* carrying v0.23.0, then move all three at once — not "upgrade what's already available and catch up later".

Standalone daemons are unaffected and may upgrade independently: cc-review (`com.yasyf.cc-review`), cc-patch (`com.yasyf.cc-patch.watch` / `.heal`), cc-orchestrate's pty daemons, cc-present. cc-notes has no daemon at all. cc-pool's *internal* daemons (`com.yasyf.cc-pool`, `.status.fusekit`, `.tenants`) are self-consistent because cc-pool bundles a matching fusekit — only its synckit-helper face is exposed to this hazard.

## Detection

A split shows up as a helper label owning a `daemon.records` file with **no sibling `daemon.sock`**, in either root, while the LaunchAgent is registered. Grep both generations:

    ls -d ~/com.github.yasyf.synckit.helper.* ~/.daemonkit/a/com.github.yasyf.synckit.helper.* 2>/dev/null

then check each for a socket. A label present in two generations at once is the fingerprint of a half-completed move.

See also [[a-daemonkit-consumer-migrates-when-it-ships-not-when-its-main-is-bumped]].
